title: Fault categorization ledger and SLA Sankey for inference request paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We currently have fragmented failure signals across the runtime (gateway, router, model-hosts) that make it hard to answer: why did this request fail the SLA? Is it a timeout, overload, model runtime error, or a protocol-level failure (HTTP/gRPC)? Existing dashboards show counts and traces in isolation but do not connect request path transitions to SLA outcomes.

Goal: Deliver a "ledger" data model and a Sankey-style dashboard that attributes SLA breaches and error outcomes to the dominant failure categories along the inference path. The artifact will: (1) standardize a failure taxonomy for inference requests, (2) add trace/span enrichment points and metrics emitted by gateway/router/host, (3) build an ETL that joins traces, metrics, and logs into ledger rows, and (4) ship Grafana/Honeycomb dashboards + alerting that surface per-route and per-model failure attribution.

Failure taxonomy (proposed): timeout.gateway | timeout.host | overload.queue | overload.runtime | model.error (runtime exception) | model.invalid_output | grpc.status.* | http.status.* | fallback.rate_limit | config.mismatch | validation.error. Each ledger row will contain a single dominant_failure tag plus a list of contributing_signatures.

Instrumentation plan (tracing hooks & span attributes):
- gateway span: route, api_key_hash, queue_time_ms, request_size, client_region, dominant_failure_hint (if immediate 4xx/5xx)
- router span: selected_cluster, routing_policy, kv_cache_hit (bool), batching_batch_id, queue_length_at_pickup
- model-host span: model_name, model_variant, gpu_util_pct, token_count_in, token_count_out, runtime_error_code, runtime_error_message (scrubbed), grpc_status, http_status
- cross-cutting: correlation_id, path_index (sequence number), sampled_for_ledger (bool)

Metrics/log pipeline:
- Traces via Honeycomb (trace-enriched spans).
- Metrics via Prometheus exporters on router and model-host; emit histograms for queue_time and inference_latency by model_variant and route.
- Logs to Loki/Datadog with structured fields failure_signature and retry_attempts.
- ETL job (Spark/Flink) runs hourly to materialize ledger rows into ClickHouse/BigQuery table used by Grafana. Ledger schema will be row-oriented flat (timestamp, request_id, route, model, dominant_failure, failure_count_vector, latency_ms_p50_p95_p99, sla_breached_bool).

Dashboards and visualizations:
- SLA Sankey (primary): request ingress -> router decisions -> host variant -> SLA outcome; link thickness = request count; color by dominant_failure. Clicking a path filters to sample traces.
- Failure signature heatmap: top 25 failure signatures across routes/models and their p95 latency.
- Temporal series: latency percentiles split by failure class (timeout vs overload vs model error).
- Top N trace samples panel with direct Honeycomb links and prefilled query using correlation_id.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Taxonomy doc published (Confluence): https://go.redwoodinc/confluence/OBS-91234-taxonomy
- Instrumentation merged: gateway/router/host emit required span attributes (PRs merged): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789
- ETL job producing ledger rows into analytics dataset; sample dataset loaded with last 7 days of data.
- Grafana dashboard deployed to observability team with Sankey, heatmap, and timeseries panels and at least two saved filters (by route, by model). Link: https://grafana.redwoodinc/d/obs/sankey-faults
- Runbook updated with how to drill from Sankey to trace and how to escalate model-runtime errors to inference-sre.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Sankey rendering for very large cardinality: we'll cap to top routes/models and provide a "others" bucket; ability to pivot to per-model view remains TBD.
- Ledger frequency: hourly vs 10m; hourly is cheaper but reduces near-real-time utility. We'll target hourly for MVP and evaluate 10m for P1.
- Storage: ClickHouse recommended for fast joins; BigQuery recommended for long-term retention. Implement ClickHouse-backed dashboard for interactive filtering.

Stakeholders: Observability (Miguel O.), Runtime (Priya Singh), Serving (Luca Moretti), Product (Jamal Reed), SRE on-call.

Rollout plan:
1) Instrumentation PRs in dev/staging; smoke test with sandbox traces (week 1)
2) ETL skeleton to produce ledger rows from staging traces (week 2)
3) Dashboard skeleton + UX review with PM/Design (week 3)
4) Gradual rollout to prod with 1-week lookback validation (week 4)

Notes: include scrubbing rules for runtime_error_message to avoid PII. Ensure security review if runtime_error_message retention > 30 days.
